subject: Essential packages for packrat/package dev workflow in system library cause "unexpected" warning

messages.author: d763070a68ca6a43
messages.subject: Essential packages for packrat/package dev workflow in system library cause "unexpected" warning
parts:
Hi guys,

In order to use packrat in the first place, (on a completely fresh R installation) I ran

> install.packages("devtools")
> devtools::install_github("rstudio/packrat")

Thus, packrat and devtools are now part of my system library.

When I go ahead and create an R package project with RStudio and check 'use packrat with this project', packrat will complain that certain packages (and its dependencies) are part of the system library and should be reinstalled. 

WARNING: It appears you have non-system packages installed in your system library.
Packrat relies on only 'base' and 'recommended' R packages being installed in the system library.

Please delete and reinstall the following packages:
- bitops, devtools, digest, evaluate, httr, manipulate, memoise, packrat, RCurl, rstudio, stringr, testthat, whisker

While this generally makes sense, I think it would be worth considering taking 'packrat' and 'devtools' (including its dependencies) off this check list as they have kind of an "global enabling character" for the entire packrat and/or package dev workflow.

Best regards,
Janko

messages.author: ab0d2be2ea8dabe8
messages.subject: Re: Essential packages for packrat/package dev workflow in system library cause "unexpected" warning
parts:
Hi Janko,

I think we need to improve the language we use here, since this has been a common point of confusion But to explain the situation, there are typically two places where packages will live (two libraries):

1. The 'system' library, as specified by .Library -- for example, on my system, I see:

> .Library
[1] "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Resources/library"

This will likely point to a library alongside your R installation on Windows. You can see the packages within here with:

> installed.packages(.Library)

You will see a large set of R packages that come bundled with R.

Then there is the 'user' library, which is found with .libPaths(). For example, I see:

> .libPaths()
[1] "/Users/kevin/Library/R/3.2/library"                            
[2] "/Library/Frameworks/R.framework/Versions/3.2/Resources/library"

That first library is my 'user' library, the second is the system library. These are the places where packages are looked up when e.g. 'library(stats)' is called.

Packrat currently requires (for Windows) that only 'base' packages live within the 'system' library (because otherwise, we break isolation as those packages you see in the warning are universally available across projects). We have some migration scripts for moving any user packages in that system library to a user library, but we are also investigating whether we can avoid this problem altogether.

You can try:

    packrat:::migrate_packages()

to clean up the system library (it will re-install those packages in a user library), or wait for us to investigate this.

Thanks,
Kevin
